name: Rhododendron Stem Borer Infestation
symptoms: Wilting or drooping leaves on individual branches Sudden dieback of stems Small holes on stems where adults lay eggs Frass (sawdust-like material) near holes Stems becoming hollow or weakened Branches breaking or dying
description: Rhododendron stem borer is a beetle whose larvae bore inside plant stems. The larvae tunnel through stems, disrupting water and nutrient flow, which causes wilting and death of branches.
management: Inspect stems regularly for egg-laying holes Prune and destroy infested stems Maintain plant health to reduce susceptibility
prevention: Regular monitoring during the growing season Remove and destroy infected stems early Avoid planting heavily infested nursery plants
